claim_limits: All account, device, operating-system, proxy, project, and incident facts are fictional synthetic user reports, not verified facts about a real person or device.
Seven actual responses from three separate synthetic conversations are retained without editing. All user turns were frozen before generation; each follow-up was supplied only when its turn arrived.

The supplied source scope was the pinned shipped Skill and ordinary references. The source boundary was instruction-enforced, not physical isolation; this does not prove inaccessible files or an isolated process.
No interview helper was invoked in these conversations. Separate normalized runtime evidence must not be attributed to these responders.

Source-reading provenance is responder-reported from retained call records, not an independently exported complete tool transcript. One source-read result omitted 329 tokens of cleanup material; that omitted text was not reread or claimed as read. Pinned full files do not imply every section was read.
Acceptance is limited to original T22/T25 in these frozen L+C scenarios. Seven observed outputs are not a guarantee for unseen prompts or future stochastic responses.

Normalized helper input/state/question assertions do not parse user prose or generate the seven retained replies. I/O sentinels are not an operating-system sandbox; module and fixture loading occur outside their boundary.

No native, current external service/account, actual client/network, official procedure, repair, recovery or cleanup-operation acceptance. Mac/Windows fixture labels establish normalized logic only; T04 and adjacent cases remain outside this decision.

Integrity regression checks retained evidence and current source identity; it does not rerun or generate model responses. Relevant source drift requires renewed semantic review, not automatic hash refresh.
